newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslavia sees ex-Yugoslav free trade zones soon.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslavia sees ex-Yugoslav free trade zones soon.

text.p: Yugoslavia hopes to soon set up free trade regimes with Bosnia and Croatia just as it did with Macedonia last month, making the first steps towards a regional customs union, the daily Nasa Borba said on Thursday.
"On Yugoslavia's part, there are no obstacles for such cooperation to be renewed as soon as possible," Yugoslav Prime Minister Radoje Kontic was quoted by the paper as saying.
Kontic referred to cooperation with "old partners in Bosnia-Herzegovina, not only in the Bosnian Serb Republic, but also in the Moslem-Croat Federation."

Kontic said the creation of a free trade zone with Macedonia had opened prospects for reviving full cooperation and that he expected certain free trade regimes "comparatively soon" with Croatia as well.
"The establishing of economic cooperation on the territory of former Yugoslavia is inevitable," Kontic said.
Yugoslavia and Macedonia abolished trade tariffs on most goods produced in the two countries.
Exempt are strategic Yugoslav agricultural products and livestock and certain Macedonian ferrous metallurgy products, cigarettes, buses and refrigerators, which remain on quotas.
Some independent analysts earlier this month described the move as the first step towards a regional trade union.
But Milojko Arsic of the Centre for Economic Studies CESMEKON said an ex-Yugoslav regional free trade zone was too narrow and would not contribute greatly to economic recovery.

"Although it could be stimulative to raising production, it would not be a generator of economic growth since we will probably never achieve the volume of trade we had before the breakup of former Yugoslavia," Arsic told Reuters. -- Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 2224305
